Here's my analogy for Elysium:

Imagine someone is exploring a desert in the middle of California.

They think "Man, California is a really popular state and a lot of people live in some of the big cities... imagine if this desert had water. Well, I'm sure people would move out here! And if they wanted to move out here, there would definitely need to be some roads... so I'll build the roads to the desert just in case there's ever water because then people would definitely want to build businesses... why? Because the desert is in California! So there'd obviously be a need for it."

So that person then creates a sales deck for a new community smack dab in the middle of the desert. They pitch the idea that there's enough growth elsewhere in the state that most likely they'll probably eventually find water, and it makes sense to a lot of people... because people in California like California.

And the cool part? The land in the new community is still so dang cheap! And the rest of the state is so expensive that when the people come out there, it's probably gonna boom.

So they buy the cheap land, and start building businesses because there were roads to get there.

And while the businesses are being built the community IS booming.

The people that bought the land struck gold!

Then slowly but surely, the building stops... and the people that were building have no reason to be there anymore because their job is finished... and then, nobody is left in the community.

Why?

Because they built it before they ever found the water.

They built it in anticipation that one day they might.

And that was enough for a bit... but at the end of the day, they're still in a desert and nobody is going to go out there unless there's an actual need to do it.

So, the roads still exist.

The empty buildings still exist.

But they slowly decay until people forget they ever did.

I think people are forgetting how strong cash cat’s narrative actually is (given it’s the first true runner of any company with that narrative)

Cash Cat was literally one of the original names considered for Robinhood before it became what it is today, it’s not just another random meme that launched on the chain

We’ve also seen clear interest from the Robinhood team and eco towards CASHCAT which I think is being seriously overlooked

Another thing I think people aren’t realizing is that Robinhood is genuinely one of the only platforms that can compete with Binance when it comes to producing massive runners

The amount of retail users, distribution and attention these platforms can bring is on a completely different level compared to most ecosystems

I don’t think the first Robinhood run was anywhere near its full potential, if anything it was ruined before it could even properly develop because of all the drama and unnecessary rotation

And that’s exactly why I think there’s an opportunity here

If Robinhood gets another wave of attention and liquidity, why wouldn’t people rotate back into one of the original runners that already has an established narrative and recognition from the eco?

CASHCAT already proved it could lead, and just because AI took over the attention for a while doesn’t mean the original narrative suddenly became irrelevant

I also think people underestimate how important it is for a meme to actually have a connection to the platform it’s trading on rather than just being another random animal with no story behind it

Obviously this all depends on Robinhood actually getting another proper run, but I think the risk/reward here is extremely interesting

Everyone’s so focused on chasing whatever is moving right now that they’re completely overlooking what could potentially be one of the more obvious plays if Robinhood picks up again

I genuinely think Robinhood has another massive run in it and CASHCAT is one of my bets for that scenario
